title: Naval Topic 5 生词 · 单词卡

cards.ex: An exercise is something you do on purpose to practice or train. A thought exercise is a small game you play in your head to think in a new way. It can also mean working out your body.
exs: Here's a fun exercise: write down three good things from today.
I do breathing exercises when I feel stressed.

src.t: There’s a little thought exercise I like to do which is,

cards.zh: 完全准确的；一模一样的
cards.ex: Exact means completely correct, with no difference at all. The exact position means the very same place you were in back then. We often say the exact same.
exs: I have the exact same phone as you.
What's the exact time of your appointment?

src.t: you can go back into your own life and try to put yourself in the exact position you were in five years ago, ten years ago, fifteen years ago, twenty years ago.

cards.ex: An objective is a goal, something you want to get or reach. It is like goal, but it sounds a little more serious and clear. Naval asks what your objectives were back then.
exs: My main objective this year is to get more regular clients.
What's the objective of this meeting?

src.t: You try to remember who was I with, what was I doing, what was I feeling, what were my emotions, what were my objectives,

cards.zh: 把（人/东西）从一个地方带到另一个地方
cards.ex: To transport means to move someone or something from one place to another. Here, transport yourself back means to imagine you are back in that time. It is like taking your mind on a trip.
exs: This song always transports me back to high school.
The boxes were transported by truck.

src.t: and really try to transport yourself back and see if there’s any advice you’d give yourself, anything you’d do differently.

cards.ex: To pretend means to act like something is true when it isn't. Naval says don't pretend you could go back and buy Bitcoin. Kids often pretend to be animals or superheroes.
exs: He pretended he didn't hear me.
Let's pretend we're on vacation tonight.

src.t: Now you don’t have new information, don’t pretend you could have gone back and bought a stock or bought Bitcoin or whatever,

cards.ex: A stock is a small part of a company that you can buy. If the company does well, your stock can go up in value. People buy stocks to make money over time.
exs: She bought some Apple stock years ago.
Stock prices went down today.

src.t: Now you don’t have new information, don’t pretend you could have gone back and bought a stock or bought Bitcoin or whatever,

cards.ex: In terms of means when we talk about a certain part or side of something. In terms of your temperament means thinking only about your personality. It helps you focus on one point.
exs: In terms of price, this salon is great.
How's the new job in terms of hours?

src.t: but just knowing what you know now in terms of your temperament and a little bit of age-related experience, how would you have done things differently?

cards.zh: 性情；脾气（情绪倾向和反应方式）
cards.ex: Your temperament is your natural personality, how you usually feel and react. Some people have a calm temperament, and some get angry fast. It's the way you are inside.
exs: My cat has a very calm temperament.
She has the right temperament for working with nervous clients.

src.t: but just knowing what you know now in terms of your temperament and a little bit of age-related experience, how would you have done things differently?

cards.ex: Related means connected to something. Age-related experience means experience that comes with getting older. We often say work-related or stress-related.
exs: I get a lot of work-related emails.
Are these two problems related?

src.t: but just knowing what you know now in terms of your temperament and a little bit of age-related experience, how would you have done things differently?

cards.ex: Worthwhile means good enough to spend your time, money or effort on. A worthwhile exercise is one that really helps you. If something is worthwhile, you won't regret doing it.
exs: The lash course was expensive, but totally worthwhile.
It's worthwhile to ask clients for reviews.

src.t: I think it’s a worthwhile exercise to do.

cards.zh: 内部的；内心的（↔ external 外部的）
cards.ex: Internal means inside, inside your body, your mind or a group. Internal suffering is pain you feel inside, in your thoughts and feelings. The opposite is external, which means outside.
exs: She stayed calm, but there was a lot of internal stress.
Internal problems in a team can slow everything down.

src.t: For me, I would have done everything the same except I would have done it with less anger, less emotion, less internal suffering because that was optional. It wasn’t necessary.

cards.ex: External means outside, coming from outside you or outside a group. External problems are things like bad weather or a rude customer. It is the opposite of internal.
exs: Don't let external noise ruin your mood.
This cream is for external use only.

cards.ex: At least means not less than a certain amount, or the minimum. It can also mean something is still good even if things aren't perfect. Chris says do the job at least peacefully.
exs: I need at least two hours for a full set.
At least try it once.

src.t: And I would argue that someone who can do the job at least peacefully, but maybe happily, is gonna be more effective than someone who has unnecessary emotional turmoil.

cards.ex: Turmoil is a state of big confusion, worry or trouble. Emotional turmoil means your feelings are very upset and messy. A country or a mind can be in turmoil.
exs: After the breakup, I was in turmoil for weeks.
The company was in turmoil after the boss left.

src.t: And I would argue that someone who can do the job at least peacefully, but maybe happily, is gonna be more effective than someone who has unnecessary emotional turmoil.

cards.ex: Miserable means very unhappy or very uncomfortable. Miserable successes means you won, but you felt bad the whole time. Bad weather can also be miserable.
exs: I felt miserable when I had the flu.
It's cold and rainy, just miserable outside.

src.t: Well, you end up with a series of miserable successes, right?
